statement: Where the compiled Lab publication is read from. The publication carries pinned schema bytes, input ownership, retained examples and authority pins for each published subject. This workbench consumes it; it does not author it.

publication.note: Regeneration checks source bytes, schema pins, the fixture digest, the provider-input binding and the exact fixture allow-list before writing a publication.

governance.note: The publication supplies application policy. It is not registered estate authority and it does not grant managed admission or remote authentication.

browserMaySubmit: editable values keyed by declared pointer
browserMayNotSubmit: an endpoint or subject outside the publication
serverResponsibilities: construct canonical input from ownership declarations
check authority pins before loading the executing plan
validate the returned outcome against the retained schema

refusalCodes.INVOCATION_BINDING_STALE: The pinned plan no longer matches the selected authority.
refusalCodes.INVOCATION_BINDING_REFUSED: An unlisted identity, or a preparation request that is not permitted.

commandBoundary.note: Reproduced from the Lab's own ownership policy so the workbench adapter can be checked against it. The loopback command service independently applies the same policy, so a direct command request cannot forge fixture inventory either.

executionSemantics.note: The deployed pilot is synchronous and deliberately preserves uncertainty. It has no durable asynchronous run-status service, which is why run acceptance is proposed as a separate protocol rather than assumed to exist.
